transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Avery Clark (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions), Ethan Reeves (Lyon - Lead ML Eng), Sofia Martinez (Lyon - Infra), Rajesh Iyer (Lyon - CTO), Priya Nair (Lyon - Security)

Summary:
Lyon Financials is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and Dedicated usage. Primary focus: p95 latency targets for streaming responses, sustained concurrency (up to 1k concurrent sessions), peak token/sec throughput for batch scoring, and private deployment considerations (VPC peering, KMS, audit logs). They want a realistic benchmark plan and documentation to bring to procurement and security.

Topics covered:
- Current infra and token/sec needs
- p95 latency SLOs and cold vs warm starts
- Concurrency patterns and burst behavior
- Streaming vs non-streaming workloads
- Benchmark plan and required artifacts
- Security/compliance questions (SOC2, KMS, VPC)

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're excited to chat through your latency and throughput goals with Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:08] Ethan: Hi Ethan here, lead ML Eng at Lyon. We're prototyping doc ingestion + real-time summaries for traders, low latency is critical.
[00:15] Priya: Priya from security, I'll just be listening for compliance details.
[00:20] Maya: Maya, SE on the Redwood side — I'll drive the benchmark discussion and technical Qs.
[00:26] Rajesh: Rajesh, CTO. Short timeline, procurement by end of March ideally.
[00:32] Jordan: Jordan, solutions — will follow up on pricing and rollout options.

[00:45] Maya: Cool, can you give a quick sense of traffic? p95 target, concurrency, token lengths?
[00:50] Ethan: Sure. Typical session is a streaming chat to summarize docs, avg request 150 tokens, but spikes to 800-1200 tokens for long docs. We need p95 under 300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and under 800ms for typical 150-token streams. For longer responses maybe up to 1.2s p95 acceptable. Concurrency: baseline 200 concurrent users, peaks to 1,000 concurrent.
[01:20] Sofia: Also we do batch scoring overnight - that's 10M tokens at ~5k qps for embeddings but that's separate. For generation batch runs we need tokens/sec throughput of roughly 50k tokens/sec sustained.
[01:35] Maya: Got it. Are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or private?
[01:38] Ethan: Ideally hosted for quick start but Dedicated for predictable latency once in prod. Private may be required for some regulated accounts.
[01:45] Jordan: We typically do hybrid: start hosted, run benchmarks, then move to Dedicated with VPC peering if needed.

[02:00] Maya: On p95 latency, a couple of clarifications — are your p95 targets measured end-to-end from client to response or only inference time?
[02:06] Ethan: End-to-end from client. Network is low-latency within us, but your hosted api region matters. For Dedicated we'd like intra-VPC targets.
[02:14] Maya: Ok. For streaming we measure time-to-first-token and sustained per-token latency for the subsequent tokens; p95 is often dominated by TTF. Cold starts (cold model in cache) can add 100-400ms depending on model size and quant. We can provide cold vs warm numbers in the benchmark.
[02:34] Ethan: That's useful — our SLO is specifically p95 time-to-first-token < 300ms for small prompts.

[03:00] Rajesh: What hardware would you recommend for 1k concurrency with those p95s?
[03:05] Maya: For the profile you described, a Dedicated pool of A100-80GB class equivalents with model quantization (8-bit where acceptable) and intelligent batching should do. We typically size nodes and autoscale such that requests are routed to hot cache nodes to avoid KV misses. For hosted we'd route by region and can guarantee baseline throughput but not the same isolation as Dedicated.
[03:30] Ethan: When you say KV misses, do you mean KV cache for the attention states? We've seen spikes when contexts are large.
[03:36] Maya: Yes, KV cache. Large context switching can evict caches; we recommend pinning hot models and using prefix caching for recurrent queries to traders.

[04:15] Sofia: For benchmarks, we need token/sec numbers for: 1) 150-token streaming with 200-1k concurrency, 2) 800-1200 token requests, and 3) batch sustained throughput. Can you run a concurrent streaming scenario?
[04:30] Maya: Yes we'll run both streaming and non-streaming. For streaming we'll look at time-to-first-token p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec per GPU. We'll include cold vs warm and different quant levels.
[04:40] Ethan: Also include request/response size overhead and per-token cost so procurement can model TCO.
[04:45] Jordan: We'll add cost per 1M tokens estimates for hosted vs dedicated reserved pricing.

[05:00] Priya: Security questions — KMS for customer-managed keys, audit logs, SSO/SAML, network topology?
[05:06] Maya: We support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated via integration; Hosted supports envelope encryption and Redwood-managed KMS by default, with enterprise options for CMKs. We also provide audit logs, per-route RBAC, and SAML SSO.
[05:20] Priya: For VPC peering, will you support private endpoints and egress control?
[05:24] Maya: Yes Dedicated and Private support VPC peering, private links, and we can restrict egress via NAT or custom routes. We'll share network diagram.

[06:00] Ethan: Any notes on streaming libraries? We saw references to function calling and tool-calls; does that affect latency?
[06:07] Maya: Function-calling can add overhead if it involves sync calls to external tools; function call outputs are streamed similarly but you may see slight increases in TTF. We'll instrument that in the benchmark.

[07:00] Rajesh: What about fallback behavior if capacity is constrained? We can't have traders blocked.
[07:08] Jordan: Redwood supports smart routing and fallbacks to smaller model variants or cross-region routing to keep requests served; config is policy-driven. We'll demo canary fallback flows in the next session.

[09:00] Maya: I'll outline the benchmark matrix:
- Streaming short prompts (<=128 tokens): 200, 500, 1k concurrency runs, measure TTF p50/p95/p99, sustained tokens/sec
- Streaming medium prompts (150 tokens): same concurrencies
- Long prompts (800-1200 tokens): lower concurrency (50, 200) to measure sustained throughput and memory behavior
- Batch throughput: sustained CPU/GPU runs to hit 50k tokens/sec target and show scaling
- Cold vs warm cache runs, quantization variants: fp16, 8-bit

[09:45] Ethan: Sounds good. For the 1k concurrency run what client-side tooling do you need? We currently use gRPC streaming from our frontend through an internal proxy.
[09:55] Maya: We'll need your client workload generator or we can script with wrk/grpc-bench. For accurate TTF we prefer running a generator inside your VPC or in same region to avoid network noise. If you can run inside your infra that's ideal, otherwise we run from Redwood Dedicated test harness.

[10:30] Sofia: Any data residency concerns? We have EU traders so region routing matters.
[10:34] Maya: We can pin regions per route and ensure data isolation on Dedicated/Private. Hosted keeps EU data in EU regions when requested.

[11:10] Priya: We'll need SOC2 certs and a network diagram; also evidence of KMS integration and audit log formats.
[11:15] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 report and a sample network diagram + KMS integration guide to the follow-up.

[12:00] Ethan: One operational question — how do you handle autoscaling and burst capacity without violating p95?
[12:06] Maya: We support predictive autoscaling policies and reserved burst capacity in Dedicated; routing policies will prefer hot nodes and probation nodes for new model versions to avoid cold-start spikes. We'll share recommended autoscale configs.

[13:00] Rajesh: About pricing — do you have examples for 3-month pilot vs 12-month committed?
[13:05] Jordan: We'll provide a matrix with hosted per-token and Dedicated reserved monthly pricing with commit tiers; 12-month gives roughly 20-30% discount depending on commit. Exact numbers in follow-up.

[14:00] Ethan: For the benchmark CSVs, include columns: timestamp, request_id, client_rtt_ms, ttf_ms, tokens_generated, model_variant, gpu_util, p95_calc.
[14:10] Maya: Yes we'll provide raw csvs plus an executive summary sheet.

[15:00] Priya: Any PII leakage risk in logs? We need redaction options.
[15:05] Maya: Logs can be configured to redact payloads or retain metadata only for audit; Private deployments give you full control.

[16:00] Rajesh: Ok let's recap next steps.
[16:06] Avery: Recap: SE runs benchmarks (streaming + batch) and shares csvs; AE shares pricing and contract examples; Redwood to share SOC2 and network diagram; customer to provide expected SLO doc and internal workload generator access. Schedule deep-dive after benchmarks.
[16:25] Ethan: Confirmed. We'll try to provide workload generator and access details by 2027-02-17.
[16:32] Priya: We'll review SOC2 and KMS details with legal.

[17:00] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep technical session.
[17:05] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll get the benchmark plan out by EOD and follow up on dates.
